212  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

of Prof. R. R. Halsell, Mr. Ben Halsell of Bonham—heightened the enthusiasm so much that the reminiscent ex-students were loath to quit singing. But the program was full and had to move fast.

    Mr. W. P. Carter, president of the Savoy School Board, gave a word of greeting.

    One of the most enjoyable surprises to the ex-students, as during the day it had been secretly planned between Mrs. J. B. May and the grandchildren of the founders. About twenty of them gathered around the microphone and gave this toast in animated fashion:

            Rah  Rah  Rah
            Rah  Rah  Rah
            Rah  Rah  Rah
        Savoy College Exes
        Gathered here from over Texas
        To honor old Savoy College,
        The place where we received your knowledge,
        Halsell! Halsell! Halsell!
        Hurr-ah! Hurr-ah!
            OUR DEAR PRESIDENT!

    Reminiscent talks of Old Savoy Days were made by Judge J. Benton Maxey of Atoka, Oklahoma; Judge Lee A. Clark of Greenville, Texas; Mr. Jno. M. Gist of Odessa, Texas; Judge W. E. McMahon of Mexico City; Judge N. E. Peak of Greenville, Texas; Mr. Jim J. Gallagher of Waco, Texas; and others. These stories ranged from humorous references to "the boy in the apple tree" in the old "Blue-Back" to poems of touching sentiment.

    An effective rendition of songs, made the more sentimental by the special setting, was given by Miss Mary Alice Pritchett, daughter of former Professor E. H. Pritchett. Mrs. E. H. Pritchett, herself a former student and teacher, was present and assisted her daughter at the piano, but becoming rather touched by the occasion, eventually gave way to Miss Mary Alice Pritchett.

    Coming next on the program as a humorous contrast, was the "Lew" Reynolds, who gave a recitation of everybody's classic poem, "My Breeches, Oh, My Sunday Breeches!"
